# Implementation Plan: Gated Copilot-first background sub-agent detector for the crews progress-bg gate (D-002)

<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-bg-gate-recognize-background-subagents"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-bg-gate-recognize-background-subagents/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The crews progress-bg gate (`hooks/stop.js` + `hooks/detect-active-bg.js`, v3.1.0+)
blocks a Copilot member's `kind=progress` turn when no async **shell** subprocess is
live at Stop time (`detectActiveBg().nonListenerCount === 0`). It does not recognize a
**Copilot background `task` sub-agent** (e.g. a Phase-5a code-review agent the member
launched and is legitimately polling) as genuine async work — so a member waiting on a
long sub-agent is forced into a synchronous in-turn wait. This plan adds the sub-agent as
a NEW, first-class detector signal source (the "third category" the v3.3.0
structural-completeness argument missed), so a *pending, still-running* sub-agent counts
as active background work — but ONLY behind a stable start→done correlation key, an
operator-only `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS` env knob (`off`/`probe`/`on`, default `off`),
and Copilot-only scope. It re-introduces **no** model-controllable bypass: the v3.3.0
no-self-attestation invariant is fully preserved (the env var is the only enable seam).

A read-only Phase-0 transcript probe done during planning (capturing this very plan
session's own Copilot `events.jsonl` while a background `task` sub-agent ran start→done)
already **confirmed feasibility**: the sub-agent emits a pre-Stop `subagent.started`
event and a durable `subagent.completed` event, both keyed by the same `toolCallId` — a
near-perfect mirror of the existing shell-async `tool.execution_start mode:async` ↔
`system.notification shell_completed` pairing keyed by `shellId`. The implementation's
STORY 1 still re-confirms this with a committed fixture against a real Phase-5a-style
sub-agent; if (contrary to the probe) the start event or correlation key turns out to be
absent, the task **collapses to D-001** — ship the status-quo synchronous-wait policy
(clearer block message + AGENTS.md guidance) instead of an unsafe detector.

### Phase-0 probe schema (CONFIRMED, planning-time, read-only)
A background `task` sub-agent writes to the parent member's `events.jsonl`:

| moment | event | key fields | correlation key |
|---|---|---|---|
| launch | `tool.execution_start` | `toolName:"task"`, `arguments.mode:"background"`, `arguments.{name,agent_type,prompt}` | `toolCallId` |
| launch | `subagent.started` | `agentName` (agent TYPE, e.g. "explore"), `agentDisplayName`, `agentDescription` | `toolCallId` (same id) |
| launch (TRAP) | `tool.execution_complete` | `success:true`, `result.content:"Agent started in background with agent_id: …"`, `toolTelemetry.properties.execution_mode:"background"`, `toolTelemetry.restrictedProperties.agent_id` | `toolCallId` — fires AT LAUNCH, **NOT a done signal** |
| completion | `subagent.completed` | `agentName`, `model`, `totalToolCalls`, `totalTokens`, `durationMs` | `toolCallId` (same id) — durable DONE signal |
| completion | `system.notification` | `kind.type:"agent_completed"`, `status:"completed"`, `agentType` | `agentId` (the human task name) — secondary signal |

**Correlation key = `toolCallId`**, present on both `subagent.started` and
`subagent.completed`. The `tool.execution_complete` at launch is the same false-completion
trap the shell path documents and must be ignored. The `system.notification agent_completed`
is keyed by `agentId` (not `toolCallId`), so it is a *secondary* corroborating signal only.
(STORY 1 must additionally probe a **failed/cancelled** sub-agent to learn whether
completion carries a non-`completed` status or a distinct event type — see Risk #2.)

### Technical Constraints
- **No model-controllable bypass (v3.3.0 invariant).** The knob is read ONLY from
  `process.env.CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS`. No `parseTurnReports`/tag/attribute/
  summary/assistant-text path may reach the new signal source. A member cannot mutate the
  parent Copilot process env from inside a turn, so the env knob is not a self-attest seam.
- **`CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_GATE=off` stays the top-level whole-gate kill switch** (unchanged).
- **`off` must be byte-identical to today** — no new log line, no decision change, and the
  `detectActiveBg()` return object must be deep-equal to the pre-change shape (no new keys)
  when the sub-agent knob is unset/`off` (see AC-5).
- **Current failure semantics (corrected).** Only the ABSENCE of a transcript PATH skips the
  gate (`stop.js:1159-1160`). A missing/unreadable/empty transcript FILE returns
  `{activeCount:0, nonListenerCount:0}` (`detect-active-bg.js:228`), so the gate BLOCKS on it
  today. The sub-agent path must preserve this: an unreadable/empty transcript contributes no
  sub-agent activity (block), never a pass.
- **Fail-toward-block asymmetry (precise rule in "Sub-agent liveness rule" below).** The
  existing shell path is permissive (ambiguous timestamps bias toward "keep active"/pass). The
  sub-agent path is STRICTER: a sub-agent counts active ONLY on a recognized start
  (`subagent.started` / `task` launch) with a parseable `start.ts ≤ asOf` AND no recognized
  terminal event ≤ asOf. An OPEN correlated start with no terminal yet IS active (that is the
  AC-2 still-running case — NOT a fail-toward-block case). The fail-toward-block cases are:
  missing/unparseable start ts, a terminal event that cannot be correlated to a start, an
  unrecognized event shape, and an optional stale-start TTL — all contribute ZERO. See the
  truth table below for every case.
- **Parent-session only.** Crews hooks already skip subagent contexts (hook input carrying
  `agent_id`/`agent_type`); the detector inspects the parent member's transcript. No change
  to that skip.
- **Tolerant parsing.** Keep the malformed-JSONL-line-skip style; tolerate a torn final line.

## Approach

### Architecture
Add the sub-agent as a **parallel signal source** inside `detect-active-bg.js`, mirroring
the shell-async structure but with stricter (fail-toward-block) semantics and a dedicated
event family. The tool-name recognition (`task`) lives in the harness-aware seam
(`listener-protocol.js`) — NOT a runtime translation adapter — so a future D-003 cross-engine
extension (Claude `Task`, codex `spawn_agent`) adds names to the same seam. The new signal
is consumed by the `stop.js` gate only when the operator opts in via the new env knob.

### Sub-agent terminal signal (baseline = the probe-confirmed `subagent.completed`)
The ONLY authoritative terminal signal in the baseline is **`subagent.completed`**, keyed by
`toolCallId` (the same id as `subagent.started`) — probe-confirmed, no bridge needed. Treat it
as terminal regardless of any `status` field. The `system.notification {kind.type:"agent_completed"}`
(agentId-keyed) is dropped from the baseline (it would require a `toolCallId↔agentId` bridge
parsed out of the launch-time `tool.execution_complete`, which adds complexity for no
additional safety while `subagent.completed` is authoritative); it is a documented follow-up
only if STORY 1's fixture proves `subagent.completed` is sometimes absent on a real run.
`tool.execution_complete` for a `task` is **launch metadata only** (it fires at launch,
`execution_mode:'background'`, `result.content:"Agent started in background…"`); it must NEVER
be treated as a terminal signal. STORY 1 additionally probes a **cancelled/failed** sub-agent:
if `subagent.completed` (or a sibling `subagent.*` terminal event) is emitted on that path too,
extend the terminal recognizer to it; if a failed sub-agent emits NO terminal event, that is
the crashed-no-completion residual risk handled by the optional stale-start TTL below.

### Sub-agent liveness rule (truth table — the source of truth for AC-2..AC-4)
`isSubagentActiveAt(start, terminal, asOf, ttlMs?)` for one `toolCallId`:

| # | transcript state for the toolCallId | decision | maps to |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | recognized `subagent.started`, parseable `start.ts ≤ asOf`, NO recognized terminal (or terminal.ts > asOf) | **ACTIVE** (pass) | AC-2 open live start |
| 2 | recognized start + recognized `subagent.completed` (any status), `terminal.ts ≤ asOf` | **inactive** (block) | AC-3 already-completed |
| 3 | recognized start, `start.ts` missing/unparseable | **inactive** (block) | AC-4 malformed start |
| 4 | recognized start, `start.ts > asOf` (not yet started as of Stop) | **inactive** (block) | AC-4 future start |
| 5 | a terminal event with NO correlatable start (foreign/uncorrelated toolCallId) | **ignored** (contributes nothing) | AC-4 uncorrelated terminal |
| 6 | unrecognized / unknown event shape | **ignored** (contributes nothing) | AC-4 unknown shape |
| 7 | open start (case 1) whose `start.ts` is older than `ttlMs` with no terminal (stale-start TTL, when configured) | **inactive** (block) | crashed-no-completion guard (Risk #2) |

`subagentActiveCount` = count of distinct `toolCallId`s in state ACTIVE. The TTL
(`CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENT_TTL_MS`, optional, default = disabled/very generous) is the
explicit answer to the "completed-but-forgotten permanent pass" risk: a sub-agent that dies
without writing `subagent.completed` stops counting active once its open start ages past the
TTL. Baseline ships with the TTL disabled (relies on probe-confirmed reliable completion +
`probe`-mode validation); operators on flaky environments can set it.

### Test determinism — pure helpers take an explicit `asOf` (resolves the wall-clock trap)
`stop.js` calls `detectActiveBg({ asOf: new Date().toISOString() })` (wall clock) — there is no
`asOf` injection seam in the gate, so a captured real fixture containing BOTH a start and a
completion timestamp will, at any future test run, look "already-completed" (both events are in
the past). Therefore:
- **Unit tests** of the pure helpers (`indexSubagentEvents`, `isSubagentActiveAt`,
  `detectActiveBg`) pass an EXPLICIT `asOf` and deterministically cover every truth-table row
  (including the between-start-and-terminal "still-running" case 1). This is where AC-2/AC-3/
  AC-4 are exhaustively proven.
- **E2E Stop-hook tests** (which use wall-clock `asOf`) follow the EXISTING shell-gate pattern
  in `progress-bg-gate.test.js`: the "still-running" fixture OMITS the terminal event (a start
  with no `subagent.completed` ⇒ active, case 1); the "already-completed" fixture includes the
  terminal event with past timestamps (case 2). No `asOf` seam is needed for E2E.
- The committed REAL fixture (`tests/fixtures/`) is the documented schema reference; it is
  exercised by a UNIT test with explicit `asOf` set between the captured start and completion
  timestamps (proving case 1 against real data), and by an E2E test using its start-only slice.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Phase-0 Copilot transcript probe + committed fixture + schema doc (STORY 1), with the
  collapse-to-D-001 decision gate.
- `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS` operator env knob (`off`/`probe`/`on`, default `off`).
- A `probe`-mode logging-only path that does not change the block decision.
- A new sub-agent signal source in `detect-active-bg.js` counting a pending sub-agent active
  ONLY behind a stable `toolCallId` start→done correlation that shows still-running at Stop.
- Fail-toward-block on unknown/uncorrelated/already-completed shapes.
- Reuse of the harness-aware tool-mention seam in `listener-protocol.js` (new
  `ASYNC_SUBAGENT_TOOL_NAMES`), NOT a runtime adapter.
- Copilot-only scope.
- Tests + AGENTS.md/CHANGELOG docs of the knob and the start→done-correlation invariant.
- crews version bump (3.10.0 → 3.11.0) via `bump-version.js`.

### Out of Scope
- Claude `Task` and codex `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent` detection (that is **D-003**, gated on
  this Copilot probe; the seam is the extension point but no other engine names are added now).
- Any runtime translation adapter between engines.
- Any new model-controllable bypass (tag/attribute/summary). v3.3.0 removed all 5; this design
  resurrects none.
- Changing the synchronous-wait fallback. With the knob `off` (default) or correlation absent,
  behavior is byte-identical to today's shell-only gate.
- Broadening the gate beyond Copilot, or touching `codex-shim.js`/`codex-stop.js`.
- Per-lead/proactive-wake changes to make a `kind=progress` checkpoint wake the lead (see
  Risk #4 — out of scope, bounds the value but does not block the detector).

## Risk Areas
1. **False-completion trap (HIGH).** `tool.execution_complete` for `task` fires at launch
   (returns `agent_id`, `execution_mode:'background'`). Pairing start↔complete by `toolCallId`
   would mark a sub-agent done the instant it launches. Mitigation: key the done side ONLY on
   `subagent.completed` (toolCallId); treat `tool.execution_complete` for `task` as launch
   metadata only, never terminal (a regression test asserts a launched sub-agent with only a
   launch-time `tool.execution_complete` is still ACTIVE — truth-table case 1).
2. **Crashed/failed sub-agent with no completion = permanent-pass risk (MEDIUM).** The planning
   probe captured only a *successful* completion (`subagent.completed`). A sub-agent that fails
   or is cancelled MIGHT emit `subagent.completed` (then it is handled — terminal regardless of
   status), MIGHT emit a sibling `subagent.*` terminal event (STORY 1 probes this; if found,
   extend the recognizer), or MIGHT emit NO terminal event at all (then its open start would
   count active forever = false-pass). Mitigations, in order: (a) baseline keys terminal on
   `subagent.completed` any-status; (b) STORY 1 attempts a cancelled/failed capture and extends
   the recognizer if a terminal event exists; (c) the optional stale-start TTL
   (`CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENT_TTL_MS`, truth-table case 7) bounds an open-forever start;
   (d) `probe` mode validates the detector's decisions against a real Phase-5a job (including a
   cancelled run) before any operator flips to `on`. `on` stays opt-in until probe-validated.
3. **`off` byte-identical regression (MEDIUM).** Any new log line or return-shape change that
   leaks into the `off` path breaks the v3.3.0 regression tests. Mitigation: gate ALL new
   logging + additive return fields on `mode !== 'off'`; a regression test asserts `off`
   output is byte-identical to pre-change for the shell-only scenarios.
4. **Bounded value / progress doesn't wake the lead (LOW, informational).** Per crews v1.6.0,
   `progress` is NOT a review-required kind and does not proactively wake the lead; a progress
   checkpoint updates only the member manifest (observability). The member is re-activated to
   collect the sub-agent result by Copilot's own sub-agent-completion notification (a new
   member turn), not by the crews listener. So progress-then-resume IS a real UX, but its
   value is bounded to "yield the turn during a long sub-agent run" rather than "signal the
   lead." Documented in Open Questions; does not block the detector.
5. **Seam-broadening safety (LOW).** Must NOT add `task` to `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES` (consumed by
   PreToolUse shell logic). The new set is separate and consumed only by the detector.
6. **`stop-allow-system-notification-boundary` interaction (LOW).** A recent
   `system.notification` exempts missing-kind ack turns (separate gate). The baseline does NOT
   consume the `agent_completed` notification, but a committed fixture/transcript may contain
   one; verify it does not perturb that boundary test's expectations (different gate / different
   turn-kind path).

## Acceptance Criteria
(Maps to the brainstorm's 7 disconfirming criteria.)
- **AC-1 (disconfirming gate).** A captured **real Copilot transcript fixture** exists under
  `tests/fixtures/` showing a background `task` START, an in-flight checkpoint, and a
  COMPLETION, with the start→done correlation key (`toolCallId`) documented — OR, if the
  fixture capture shows no pre-Stop start event and/or no stable correlation key, the task is
  closed/escalated as "D-002 infeasible → collapses to D-001" (clearer block message +
  AGENTS.md policy) instead of shipping a detector. Must be resolved before any gate-behavior
  change ships.
- **AC-2 (open live start ⇒ pass).** With `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS=on` and a transcript
  containing a `subagent.started` (parseable `start.ts ≤ asOf`) for a `toolCallId` with NO
  `subagent.completed` (truth-table case 1), and `nonListenerCount === 0`, a member's
  `kind=progress` is **allowed**. Proven at the UNIT level with explicit `asOf` between start
  and (absent) terminal, and at the E2E level with a start-only fixture slice.
- **AC-3 (already-completed ⇒ block).** Knob `on`, transcript has `subagent.started` +
  `subagent.completed` (any status) for the same `toolCallId`, both `ts ≤ asOf` (case 2), and
  `nonListenerCount === 0` ⇒ `kind=progress` is **blocked** (no completed-but-forgotten
  permanent pass). Unit (explicit `asOf` after terminal) + E2E (both events in the past).
- **AC-4 (fail-toward-block cases ⇒ block / ignore).** Knob `on`, `nonListenerCount === 0`, and
  each of these distinct states blocks `kind=progress` (unit tests, one per row; E2E for at
  least the malformed-start and uncorrelated-terminal rows):
  - missing/unparseable `start.ts` (case 3) ⇒ not active ⇒ block;
  - `start.ts > asOf` future start (case 4) ⇒ not active ⇒ block;
  - a terminal event whose `toolCallId` matches no start (case 5, uncorrelated) ⇒ ignored ⇒ block;
  - an unrecognized/unknown event shape (case 6) ⇒ ignored ⇒ block;
  - (when TTL configured) an open start older than `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENT_TTL_MS` (case 7) ⇒ block.
- **AC-5 (`off` byte-identical, precise surface).** With `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS` unset or
  `off`: (a) `detectActiveBg()`'s return object is **deep-equal** (same keys, same values) to
  the pre-change shape `{activeCount, nonListenerCount, samples, asOf}` — NO `subagent*` keys;
  (b) the `progress-bg-gate` log line has **no** `subagentMode`/`subagentActive` fields; (c) the
  block/pass decision is identical to the current shell-only detector for the existing
  scenarios (regression against the unchanged shell fixtures).
- **AC-6 (probe ⇒ log-only).** In `probe` mode the detector COMPUTES + LOGS its sub-agent
  decision (grep-able ` subagentMode=probe subagentActive=N`) but adds 0 to the effective
  active count, so the stop decision is identical to `off` for the same transcript (unit + E2E:
  an `on`-would-pass transcript still BLOCKS under `probe`).
- **AC-7 (no self-attestation).** The model **cannot** flip the knob or self-attest past the
  gate from inside a turn — the env var is the only enable seam. A test asserts a transcript
  whose assistant text / report tag carries a bypass-shaped token (e.g. `background-task`,
  `subagent-active`) does NOT change the sub-agent decision (no `parseTurnReports`/tag/
  attribute/summary/assistant-text path reaches the new signal source).
- **AC-8 (`CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_GATE=off`).** Still disables the **whole** gate exactly as before,
  regardless of `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS` (unchanged regression).
- **AC-9 (combined-count ordering).** When `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS=on` AND real shell bg
  work is present (`nonListenerCount > 0`) AND there is no sub-agent, `kind=progress` passes
  exactly as today (the sub-agent path must not regress the shell path); and when
  `nonListenerCount === 0` but an active sub-agent exists under `on`, the single combined
  decision (`effectiveActive > 0`) passes — proving the gate computes both signals before the
  one block decision (not "block on shell-count-0 first"). Unit + E2E.
- **AC-10 (invalid knob ⇒ off).** `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS` set to any value other than
  `probe`/`on` (e.g. `yes`, `1`, ``) resolves to `off` (unit test of the parser + an E2E that
  an invalid value behaves byte-identically to `off`).
- **AC-11 (build/verify).** `node tests/run.js` (from `plugins/crews/`) passes; `node --check`
  clean on changed JS; `scripts/bump-version.js 3.11.0` applied and `tests/version.test.js`
  green; the codexu root `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table shows `crews 3.11.0` after the
  lead's parent-pointer ship (lead-owned, verified at merge).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001** Phase-0 Copilot transcript probe + committed fixture + feasibility decision (HARD
  PREREQ; gates US-002..US-006; includes the collapse-to-D-001 fallback).
- **US-002** Harness-aware `task` tool-name seam (`ASYNC_SUBAGENT_TOOL_NAMES`) + the
  `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS` knob parser.
- **US-003** Sub-agent signal source in `detect-active-bg.js` (`indexSubagentEvents`,
  `isSubagentActiveAt` implementing the truth table, additive return fields), with the
  false-done trap handled and the optional stale-start TTL.
- **US-004** Wire the signal into the `stop.js` gate behind the knob (`off`/`probe`/`on`) using
  a single combined-count decision (`effectiveActive = nonListenerCount + on?subagentActiveCount:0`)
  + extended logging (mode≠off only).
- **US-005** Tests — unit (detector helpers per truth-table rows, knob parser incl. invalid→off,
  seam export) + E2E Stop-hook (AC-2..AC-10) + fixture-backed + `off` deep-equal/byte-identical
  regression.
- **US-006** Docs (`AGENTS.md` `## v3.11.0` + `CHANGELOG.md`) + plugin version bump via
  `bump-version.js 3.11.0` (plugin-local, on the submodule topic branch). Parent-repo
  bookkeeping — codexu submodule-pointer bump + root AGENTS.md active-plugin-versions table
  (`crews 3.10.0`→`3.11.0`) — is the lead's at-merge ceremony (see Files to Modify note).

## Suggested Decomposition
All six stories touch a tightly overlapping file set (`detect-active-bg.js`, `stop.js`,
`listener-protocol.js`, the shared test files, `AGENTS.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`/version files) and
US-001 is a hard feasibility prerequisite for the rest. Parallel execution is unsafe (file
conflicts + the gating dependency). Recommend a **single serial cluster**.

### Cluster: bg-subagent-detector (serial)
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=`hooks/detect-active-bg.js`, `hooks/stop.js`,
  `hooks/listener-protocol.js`, `tests/progress-bg-gate.test.js`, `tests/listener-protocol.test.js`,
  `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, version-stamp files; exclusive=none; risk=high (single-plugin,
  same-file, US-001 gates all).
- `execution_mode` rationale: Must be serialized — every story edits the same 2-3 hook files
  and shared test files, and US-001's feasibility gate must resolve before any detector code
  is written. Running stories in parallel would produce conflicting edits to the same files
  and could build a detector before the fixture proves the schema.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <plan_job_dir>/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition <plan_job_dir>/suggested-decomposition.json`
(Note: parallel handoff is offered for interface consistency, but this plan's single-cluster
serial decomposition means `--parallel` runs the one cluster serially — prefer the plain
`--from-plan` serial path.)

## Open Questions
- **Failure/cancel completion shape** (Risk #2): the planning probe captured only a successful
  completion. STORY 1 should attempt a failed/cancelled sub-agent capture; if not feasible, the
  detector's "any terminal event ⇒ done" rule is the conservative default and `on` stays
  opt-in until `probe` mode validates a cancelled run. `[INFERRED]` the failure path emits a
  `subagent.completed`/`agent_completed` with a non-`completed` status OR a sibling
  `subagent.failed`/`agent_failed` event — to be confirmed at impl.
- **Value bound** (Risk #4): does a `kind=progress` while a sub-agent runs meaningfully help,
  given progress doesn't wake the lead? The member is re-activated by Copilot's own sub-agent
  completion notification, so progress-then-resume frees the member from a long synchronous
  wait — real but bounded value. The operator chose D-002 over D-001 accepting this.
- **Probe→on promotion criteria**: how many `probe`-mode real-job validations (correct
  decisions vs ground truth, including a completed and a cancelled run) before flipping default
  guidance to `on`? Recommend documenting a manual checklist in AGENTS.md rather than auto-flipping.
